data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The rival criteria are unified by a two-level invariant: (L1) log-level append-only identity requires that no committed event is ever modified or deleted; (L2) stream-level causal identity requires that the resumption produces the same event sequence that would have been produced without interruption. Resumption is safe iff L1 holds trivially (partial fragments are non-events) AND L2 holds (causal fingerprint of last complete event matches the continuation point AND no exogenous event was interleaved). Refusal is required when L2 fails even if L1 holds, because the resumed stream would diverge from the canonical stream.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If L1 and L2 cannot be independently verified (e.g., the causal fingerprint is embedded in the event payload and a partial fragment corrupts the payload of the last complete event), the two-level decomposition fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If exogenous events are permitted between exhaustion and resumption (multi-writer log), L2 may be unachievable and refusal is the only safe option regardless of L1.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the causal fingerprint is not deterministic (e.g., depends on non-deterministic system state like thread scheduling), L2 cannot be verified and the invariant is vacuous.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"SRC_001 conflates L1 and L2: it treats barrier absence as an L1 violation, but barriers address L2 (marking the continuation point), not L1 (which is about immutability of written events). SRC_002's three conditions are an attempt at L2 but are stated too narrowly (requiring explicit barrier). The covering principle separates the two invariants: L1 is about physical integrity of the log, L2 is about logical correctness of the continuation. A partial fragment threatens neither L1 (it is not an event) nor L2 (it carries no causal weight) unless it is misinterpreted. The barrier is a sufficient mechanism for L2 but not necessary; framing-based quarantine is necessary and sufficient for L1, and fingerprint matching is necessary and sufficient for L2.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
